title: Interface-name checks rejected some AI-written code that passed behavioral tests
summary: In a post hoc analysis of AI-written code, 19 of 36 artifacts rejected solely for dropping leading underscores from parameter names passed the original hidden behavioral checks after only that name-comparison rule was bypassed. The original study kept those artifacts recorded as contract failures. The selection covers one specific failure reason in the study’s coding tasks.

source_review.scope: v1 §§9.3–9.4 coding delegation and post hoc hidden-test diagnostic

evidence.tested: A secondary offline diagnostic applied selected generated artifacts unchanged to fresh task copies, bypassing only strict parameter-name comparison, then ran the original sealed behavioral checks. No parent review or end-to-end acceptance was replayed.
evidence.unknown: This selected subset cannot estimate overall pass rates or establish that contract requirements were unnecessary in deployment. Original saved records were private and not independently auditable; passing these author-supplied checks does not prove general software correctness.
evidence.ai_role: Existing language models acting as coding workers generated artifacts assessed under an interface contract and hidden behavioral tests.
